review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

16:1.sourceText: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητάς Ἄνθρωπός τις ἦν πλούσιος ὃς εἶχεν οἰκονόμον, καὶ οὗτος διεβλήθη αὐτῷ ὡς διασκορπίζων τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ.
16:1.targetText: Jesus also said to His disciples, “There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his possessions.

groups.note: The article serves as the possessive His.
ὃς εἶχεν ("who had") is rendered whose.
ὡς ("as") introduces the charge, rendered of.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
BSB folds "and this one was accused" into the relative clause, so καί and the pronoun οὗτος have no separate English words.
BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him," the rich man) unexpressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speaker; the Greek has only the verb.

16:2.sourceText: καὶ φωνήσας αὐτὸν εἶπεν αὐτῷ Τί τοῦτο ἀκούω περὶ σοῦ; ἀπόδος τὸν λόγον τῆς οἰκονομίας σου· οὐ γὰρ δύνῃ ἔτι οἰκονομεῖν.
16:2.targetText: So he called him in to ask, ‘What is this I hear about you? Turn in an account of your management, for you cannot be manager any longer.’

groups.note: εἶπεν ("said") is rendered as the purpose to ask.
οὐ δύνῃ ("you are not able") is rendered you cannot.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:3.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ ἐν ἑαυτῷ ὁ οἰκονόμος Τί ποιήσω, ὅτι ὁ κύριός μου ἀφαιρεῖται τὴν οἰκονομίαν ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ; σκάπτειν οὐκ ἰσχύω, ἐπαιτεῖν αἰσχύνομαι.
16:3.targetText: The manager said to himself, ‘What shall I do, now that my master is taking away my position? I am too weak to dig and too ashamed to beg.

groups.note: ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ ("from me") is rendered by the possessive my.
οὐκ ἰσχύω ("I am not strong enough") is rendered I am too weak.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the two clauses; the Greek has no connective.

16:4.sourceText: ἔγνων τί ποιήσω, ἵνα ὅταν μετασταθῶ ἐκ τῆς οἰκονομίας δέξωνταί με εἰς τοὺς οἴκους ἑαυτῶν.
16:4.targetText: I know what I will do, so that after my removal from management, people will welcome me into their homes.’

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:5.sourceText: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος ἕνα ἕκαστον τῶν χρεοφειλετῶν τοῦ κυρίου ἑαυτοῦ ἔλεγεν τῷ πρώτῳ Πόσον ὀφείλεις τῷ κυρίῳ μου;
16:5.targetText: And he called in each one of his master’s debtors. ‘How much do you owe my master?’ he asked the first.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:6.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ἑκατὸν βάτους ἐλαίου. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Δέξαι σου τὰ γράμματα καὶ καθίσας ταχέως γράψον πεντήκοντα.
16:6.targetText: ‘A hundred measures of olive oil,’ he answered.  ‘Take your bill,’ said the manager. ‘Sit down quickly, and write fifty.’

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he.
In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun; BSB names the manager.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:7.sourceText: ἔπειτα ἑτέρῳ εἶπεν Σὺ δὲ πόσον ὀφείλεις; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ἑκατὸν κόρους σίτου. λέγει αὐτῷ Δέξαι σου τὰ γράμματα καὶ γράψον ὀγδοήκοντα.
16:7.targetText: Then he asked another, ‘And how much do you owe?’  ‘A hundred measures of wheat,’ he replied.  ‘Take your bill and write eighty,’ he told him.

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:8.sourceText: καὶ ἐπῄνεσεν ὁ κύριος τὸν οἰκονόμον τῆς ἀδικίας ὅτι φρονίμως ἐποίησεν· ὅτι οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου φρονιμώτεροι ὑπὲρ τοὺς υἱοὺς τοῦ φωτὸς εἰς τὴν γενεὰν τὴν ἑαυτῶν εἰσιν.
16:8.targetText: The master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly. For the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the sons of light.

groups.note: τῆς ἀδικίας ("of unrighteousness") describes the manager as dishonest.
English repeats the verb in the comparison.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:9.sourceText: Καὶ ἐγὼ ὑμῖν λέγω, ἑαυτοῖς ποιήσατε φίλους ἐκ τοῦ μαμωνᾶ τῆς ἀδικίας, ἵνα ὅταν ἐκλίπῃ δέξωνται ὑμᾶς εἰς τὰς αἰωνίους σκηνάς.
16:9.targetText: I tell you, use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves, so that when it is gone, they will welcome you into eternal dwellings.

groups.note: The command ποιήσατε ("make") is rendered as the purpose of use.
ἐκ ("by means of") is rendered with the verb use.
τῆς ἀδικίας ("of unrighteousness") is rendered worldly.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:10.sourceText: ὁ πιστὸς ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ καὶ ἐν πολλῷ πιστός ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ ἄδικος καὶ ἐν πολλῷ ἄδικός ἐστιν.
16:10.targetText: Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.

groups.note: ὁ πιστός ("the faithful one") is rendered Whoever is faithful.
The present ἐστιν ("is") is rendered will be.
ὁ … ἄδικος ("the dishonest one") is rendered whoever is dishonest.

16:11.sourceText: εἰ οὖν ἐν τῷ ἀδίκῳ μαμωνᾷ πιστοὶ οὐκ ἐγένεσθε, τὸ ἀληθινὸν τίς ὑμῖν πιστεύσει;
16:11.targetText: So if you have not been faithful with worldly wealth, who will entrust you with true riches?

groups.note: ἀδίκῳ ("unrighteous") is rendered worldly, as in 16:9.
The substantive τὸ ἀληθινόν ("the true thing") is rendered true riches.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:12.sourceText: καὶ εἰ ἐν τῷ ἀλλοτρίῳ πιστοὶ οὐκ ἐγένεσθε, τὸ ἡμέτερον τίς δώσει ὑμῖν;
16:12.targetText: And if you have not been faithful with the belongings of another, who will give you belongings of your own?

groups.note: ἀλλότριος means "belonging to another".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB follows a reading meaning "yours" here; N1904's ἡμέτερον means "ours".

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading meaning "yours" here, not N1904's ἡμέτερον ("ours").

16:13.sourceText: Οὐδεὶς οἰκέτης δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν· ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει, ἢ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει. οὐ δύνασθε Θεῷ δουλεύειν καὶ μαμωνᾷ.
16:13.targetText: No servant can serve two masters. Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.”

groups.note: οὐ δύνασθε ("you are not able") is rendered You cannot.

unmappedSource.reason: English gives the alternatives without an explanatory marker.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a two-part quantifier before the two objects.

16:14.sourceText: Ἤκουον δὲ ταῦτα πάντα οἱ Φαρισαῖοι φιλάργυροι ὑπάρχοντες, καὶ ἐξεμυκτήριζον αὐτόν.
16:14.targetText: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all of this and were scoffing at Jesus.

groups.note: BSB names Jesus for αὐτόν ("him").

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.

16:15.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ δικαιοῦντες ἑαυτοὺς ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὁ δὲ Θεὸς γινώσκει τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν· ὅτι τὸ ἐν ἀνθρώποις ὑψηλὸν βδέλυγμα ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ.
16:15.targetText: So He said to them, “You are the ones who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts. For what is prized among men is detestable before God.

groups.note: τὸ … ὑψηλόν ("the exalted thing") is rendered what is prized.
βδέλυγμα ("an abomination") is rendered detestable.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek clause has none.

16:16.sourceText: Ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται μέχρι Ἰωάνου· ἀπὸ τότε ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ εὐαγγελίζεται καὶ πᾶς εἰς αὐτὴν βιάζεται.
16:16.targetText: The Law and the Prophets were proclaimed until John. Since that time, the gospel of the kingdom of God is being preached, and everyone is forcing his way into it.

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
εὐαγγελίζεται ("is proclaimed as good news") is rendered the gospel of … is being preached.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb; the Greek clause has none.

16:17.sourceText: εὐκοπώτερον δέ ἐστιν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν παρελθεῖν ἢ τοῦ νόμου μίαν κεραίαν πεσεῖν.
16:17.targetText: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for a single stroke of a pen to drop out of the Law.

groups.note: "for" introduces the subject of the infinitive, as Mark 10:25.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:18.sourceText: Πᾶς ὁ ἀπολύων τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ γαμῶν ἑτέραν μοιχεύει, καὶ ὁ ἀπολελυμένην ἀπὸ ἀνδρὸς γαμῶν μοιχεύει.
16:18.targetText: Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery, and he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.

groups.note: ὁ … γαμῶν ("the one marrying") is rendered he who marries.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves ἀπὸ ἀνδρός ("from a husband") implicit in divorced.

16:19.sourceText: Ἄνθρωπος δέ τις ἦν πλούσιος, καὶ ἐνεδιδύσκετο πορφύραν καὶ βύσσον εὐφραινόμενος καθ’ ἡμέραν λαμπρῶς.
16:19.targetText: Now there was a rich man dressed in purple and fine linen, who lived each day in joyous splendor.

groups.note: The participle εὐφραινόμενος ("making merry") is rendered who lived … joyous.
λαμπρῶς ("splendidly") is rendered in splendor.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB turns "and he was dressed" into the participle dressed, so καί has no English word.

16:20.sourceText: πτωχὸς δέ τις ὀνόματι Λάζαρος ἐβέβλητο πρὸς τὸν πυλῶνα αὐτοῦ εἱλκωμένος
16:20.targetText: And a beggar named Lazarus lay at his gate, covered with sores

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:21.sourceText: καὶ ἐπιθυμῶν χορτασθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν πιπτόντων ἀπὸ τῆς τραπέζης τοῦ πλουσίου· ἀλλὰ καὶ οἱ κύνες ἐρχόμενοι ἐπέλειχον τὰ ἕλκη αὐτοῦ.
16:21.targetText: and longing to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.

groups.note: τῶν πιπτόντων ("the things falling") is rendered the … that fell.
ἀλλὰ καί ("but even") is rendered Even.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a noun for the participle ("what fell").
English joins the participle came to the main verb.

16:22.sourceText: ἐγένετο δὲ ἀποθανεῖν τὸν πτωχὸν καὶ ἀπενεχθῆναι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀγγέλων εἰς τὸν κόλπον Ἀβραάμ· ἀπέθανεν δὲ καὶ ὁ πλούσιος καὶ ἐτάφη.
16:22.targetText: One day the beggar died and was carried by the angels to Abraham’s side. And the rich man also died and was buried.

groups.note: The narrative formula ἐγένετο δέ ("now it came about") is rendered One day.
κόλπον ("bosom") is rendered side.

unmappedSource.reason: English does not repeat the subject αὐτόν ("him").
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:23.sourceText: καὶ ἐν τῷ Ἅιδῃ ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ, ὑπάρχων ἐν βασάνοις, ὁρᾷ Ἀβραὰμ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν καὶ Λάζαρον ἐν τοῖς κόλποις αὐτοῦ.
16:23.targetText: In Hades, where he was in torment, he looked up and saw Abraham from afar, with Lazarus by his side.

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ ("lifting up his eyes") is rendered he looked up.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle looked up to the main verb.

16:24.sourceText: καὶ αὐτὸς φωνήσας εἶπεν Πάτερ Ἀβραάμ, ἐλέησόν με καὶ πέμψον Λάζαρον ἵνα βάψῃ τὸ ἄκρον τοῦ δακτύλου αὐτοῦ ὕδατος καὶ καταψύξῃ τὴν γλῶσσάν μου, ὅτι ὀδυνῶμαι ἐν τῇ φλογὶ ταύτῃ.
16:24.targetText: So he cried out, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue. For I am in agony in this fire.’

groups.note: φωνήσας εἶπεν ("calling out, said") is rendered cried out.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:25.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ Ἀβραάμ Τέκνον, μνήσθητι ὅτι ἀπέλαβες τὰ ἀγαθά σου ἐν τῇ ζωῇ σου, καὶ Λάζαρος ὁμοίως τὰ κακά· νῦν δὲ ὧδε παρακαλεῖται σὺ δὲ ὀδυνᾶσαι.
16:25.targetText: But Abraham answered, ‘Child, remember that during your lifetime you received your good things, while Lazarus received bad things. But now he is comforted here, while you are in agony.

groups.note: English repeats the verb for Lazarus.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves ὁμοίως ("likewise") untranslated and repeats received instead.

16:26.sourceText: καὶ ἐν πᾶσι τούτοις μεταξὺ ἡμῶν καὶ ὑμῶν χάσμα μέγα ἐστήρικται, ὅπως οἱ θέλοντες διαβῆναι ἔνθεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς μὴ δύνωνται, μηδὲ ἐκεῖθεν πρὸς ἡμᾶς διαπερῶσιν.
16:26.targetText: And besides all this, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that even those who wish cannot cross from here to you, nor can anyone cross from there to us.’

groups.note: μὴ δύνωνται ("may not be able") is rendered cannot.

16:27.sourceText: εἶπεν δέ Ἐρωτῶ σε οὖν, πάτερ, ἵνα πέμψῃς αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ πατρός μου·
16:27.targetText: ‘Then I beg you, father,’ he said, ‘send Lazarus to my father’s house,

groups.note: BSB names Lazarus for αὐτόν ("him").

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
English turns the ἵνα clause into a direct command.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:28.sourceText: ἔχω γὰρ πέντε ἀδελφούς· ὅπως διαμαρτύρηται αὐτοῖς, ἵνα μὴ καὶ αὐτοὶ ἔλθωσιν εἰς τὸν τόπον τοῦτον τῆς βασάνου.
16:28.targetText: for I have five brothers. Let him warn them, so that they will not also end up in this place of torment.’

groups.note: ὅπως διαμαρτύρηται ("so that he may warn") is rendered Let him warn.
ἔλθωσιν ("come") is rendered end up.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:29.sourceText: λέγει δὲ Ἀβραάμ Ἔχουσι Μωϋσέα καὶ τοὺς προφήτας· ἀκουσάτωσαν αὐτῶν.
16:29.targetText: But Abraham replied, ‘They have Moses and the prophets; let your brothers listen to them.’

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb ending.

16:30.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Οὐχί, πάτερ Ἀβραάμ, ἀλλ’ ἐάν τις ἀπὸ νεκρῶν πορευθῇ πρὸς αὐτοὺς, μετανοήσουσιν.
16:30.targetText: ‘No, father Abraham,’ he said, ‘but if someone is sent to them from the dead, they will repent.’

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he.
πορευθῇ ("goes") is rendered is sent.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.

16:31.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ Εἰ Μωϋσέως καὶ τῶν προφητῶν οὐκ ἀκούουσιν, οὐδὲ ἐάν τις ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῇ πεισθήσονται.
16:31.targetText: Then Abraham said to him, ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead.’”

groups.note: οὐδέ ("not even") is split around the verb in English.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speaker; the Greek has only the verb.
